jobs.title: Project & Corporate Finance Lead
jobs.description:
Job Posting End Date
10-26-2026 Please note the job posting will close on the day before the posting end date.

Job Summary

AEP is seeking a finance leader with practical project finance experience and a strong grounding in corporate finance. The successful candidate will partner with business units, legal, accounting, tax, regulatory and external financing parties to structure and execute financing solutions for major infrastructure and strategic investments. The role’s primary emphasis is project finance, including evaluating bankability, allocating risk, coordinating diligence, developing financing structures and negotiating transaction terms. The position will also support corporate financing, capital structure, credit ratings, cost of capital and regulated utility finance matters.

This is a transaction execution and financial strategy role, not a cash management or treasury operations position. The ideal candidate is energized by complex transactions, cross-functional problem solving and communicating financing recommendations to senior leaders and other stakeholders.
Job Description

What You'll Do:

- Lead the structuring, evaluation and execution of project financings, including non-recourse and limited-recourse structures, construction and term debt, secured facilities, private placements, leases and other fit-for-purpose financing solutions.
- Assess project bankability and financing risk, including commercial terms, construction and completion risk, operating performance, contractual protections, counterparty strength, cash flow durability and lender requirements.
- Coordinate transaction workstreams across internal teams and external advisors, including lenders, investment banks, legal counsel, rating agencies, independent engineers and other diligence providers.
- Develop and review financial models, financing plans, sources-and-uses analyses, debt capacity assessments, sensitivity cases and recommendations that support investment and financing decisions.
- Negotiate financing terms and documentation in partnership with legal counsel and business stakeholders and translate complex provisions into clear business implications for decisionmakers.
- Execute corporate financing transactions, which may include term loans, secured or unsecured bonds, private placements, leases and other capital markets instruments.
- Advise on capital structure, cost of capital, subsidiary financing strategy and credit metrics, including support for rating agency engagement and credit analysis.
- Support financial planning and regulated utility proceedings by preparing analyses, work papers and clear explanations of financing assumptions, cost of debt and cost of capital.
- Prepare concise, decision-oriented materials for executives, the Board of Directors and other stakeholders regarding financing alternatives, transaction status, risks and recommendations.
- Provide leadership, coaching and technical guidance to Corporate Finance team members and promote effective collaboration across the organization.

What We're Looking For:

Treasury Analyst Principal (Salary Grade 9)

Education: Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting or related field with solid understanding of financial theory.

Experience: At least 4 years of relevant experience within corporate banking, debt capital markets or corporate finance with direct experience in project finance, infrastructure finance, investment banking, or at least 6 years of adjacent experience that include 1 years of direct experience in project/infrastructure finance.

Treasury Lead (Salary Grade 10)

Education: Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting or related field with solid understanding of financial theory.

Experience: At least 6 years of relevant experience within corporate banking, debt capital markets or corporate finance with direct experience in project finance, infrastructure finance, investment banking, or at least 8 years of adjacent experience that include 3 years of direct experience in project/infrastructure finance.

Additional Expectations:

The preferred talent will have
- Meaningful hands-on project finance experience is required. Relevant experience may include power, utilities, renewable energy, transmission, infrastructure or other capital-intensive sectors.
- Working knowledge of project finance structures, credit analysis, financial modeling, due diligence, financing documentation and transaction execution.
- Corporate finance experience involving capital structure, debt financing, credit ratings, cost of capital or financial planning is strongly preferred.

Where You'll Work:
- On-Site in the AEP Headquarters in Columbus, OH

What You'll Get:
- Base salary
- Annual bonus
- 401K match
- AEP Pension
- Comprehensive benefits package that aims to support and enhance the overall well-being of our employees.

jobs.title: Director Business Transformation (Special Projects)
jobs.description:
Job Posting End Date
10-19-2026 Please note the job posting will close on the day before the posting end date.

Job Summary

The Director, Business Transformation is a strategic leadership role involved in driving transformation initiatives within the Transmission organization. Reporting to the VP, Transmission Center of Excellence, this role will lead cross-functional efforts to identify process improvement opportunities, establish key performance indicators, implement innovative solutions, and enhance organizational effectiveness. The Director will serve as a key change agent, aligning transformation efforts with organizational goals, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.

Leads continuous improvement cohorts and coaches participants in development of capabilities and execution of improvement initiatives. Maintains continuous improvement community of practice. Leads special projects within Transmission at the direction of Transmission President or VP, Business Transformation.
Job Description

What You'll Do:

Strategic Transformation Leadership
- Lead the design and execution of transformation strategies aligned with the Transmission CoE vision.
- Partner with Transmission leaders to identify and prioritize high-impact transformation opportunities.

Process Optimization & Innovation
- Oversee end-to-end process improvement initiatives across transmission operations.
- Introduce and scale innovative methodologies, including Lean, Six Sigma, and Agile practices.

Performance Management
- Develop and monitor KPIs to measure transformation success and ensure alignment with strategic goals.
- Utilize data analytics to inform decision-making and track performance improvements.

Change Management
- Lead change management efforts to ensure successful adoption of new processes and technologies.
- Develop communication and training plans to support transformation initiatives.

Team & Capability Development
- Build and lead a high-performing transformation team.
- Coach and mentor staff and stakeholders on continuous improvement tools and techniques.

Stakeholder Engagement
- Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to ensure alignment and support for transformation efforts.
- Facilitate leadership workshops and progress report-outs to drive accountability and transparency.

What We're Looking For:

Education:
- Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Engineering, IT, Industrial Engineer, Operations Management, or related field.
- MBA or advanced degree preferred.

Experience:
- Minimum of 8 years of experience in utility industry.
- Proven track record of engaging in cross-functional transformation efforts in the utility or related industry.

Certifications:
- PMP, Lean, Six Sigma, or other transformation-related certifications preferred.

Skills & Attributes:
- Strong strategic thinking and leadership capabilities.
- Excellent communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills.
- Ability to navigate ambiguity and drive results in a complex organizational environment.
- Innovative mindset with a commitment to continuous improvement.

Where You'll Work:
- On-Site in AEP locations: New Albany, OH, Roanoke, VA, Corpus Christi, TX or Tulsa, OK

What You'll Get:
- Base salary
- Annual bonus
- Long-term incentive
- 401K match

jobs.title: Supply Chain Stores Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Job Posting End Date
10-19-2026 Please note the job posting will close on the day before the posting end date.

Job Summary

Manages the storeroom operations within the assigned Operating Company or Region to ensure the business needs of the applicable business unit are met in a safe and cost effective manner. Effectively partners with managers and supervisors of Stores to align material availability with construction/maintenance needs. Actively monitors Supply Chain measures to identify corrective action that are needed to ensure Supply Chain and Business Unit goals are achieved.
Job Description

What you will be doing:

- Direct the operation of the associated storerooms within the assigned Operating Company or Region.
- Recommend storeroom staffing, and enhancements to the materials flow process to management.
- Recommend policies and procedures relating to the proper control of all inventory investments and material services functions. a. SOX Compliance b. Cycle Inventories c. Inactive Material Reviews d. MSDS e. QC
- Responsible for materials management of M&S, Capital & oversite of plant Direct Charge (proper/safe storage, proper indentification, etc.)
- Direct and coordinate the Material Management functions between storerooms; act as liaison between Stores Supervisors, Accounting, Procurement, Engineering and Projects Departments.
- Develop, implement and/or assist in the development and implementation of measurements/goals of storeroom operations. Monitor the results of measures and take appropriate corrective action needed to ensure that Supply Chain and Business Unit goals are achieved.
- Ensure that storeroom operations comply with corporate and departmental policies and procedures.
- Establish effective communication channels with internal and external customers around all aspects of the catalog and Inventory Optimization.
- Support required staffing and materials in support of storm restoration, outage & project requirements of the business unit.
- Coordinates the training and development of assigned employees in a manner that aggressively migrates culture to a participative, zero harm environment.
- Development and administer safety programs that aggressively migrates the culture "mind set" to a norm of zero harm.
- Actively participate in the development and administration of training programs to ensure maximum utilization of available technology and personnel and ensure that employees have the opportunity to develop to their full potential.
- Foster an environment that embraces diversity of thinking and participative management.
- Demonstrate the highest standards of ethical behavior and support the Company's Corporate Compliance Policy.
- Carry out, within the assigned area of responsibility, the Company's program of Equal employment Opportunity, including its Affirmative Action obligations.
- Administer the company's Performance Management Review and Salary Administration programs and Management Information and Policy Manual.
- Promote and enforce the company's Accident Prevention and Safety & Health programs to migrate towards an accident free culture.
- Assume other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

What we are looking for:
- Bachelor’s degree in business administration or equivalent education and experience.
- Work Experience requirements listed below: Must have a minimum of ten (10) years business experience in Supply Chain, Distribution, Transmission or Generation positions. Minimum of three (3) years direct supervisory experience.

Other Requirements:
- Physical demand level is Sedentary
- Has responsibility for multiple facilities, Hundreds of Millions in Inventory, budget of +$100M material throughput. Position will require travel to various facilities throughout the geographic area of responsibility.
- Continuous Travel is required.
